Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume, including dimension zero. All approved ambient section instances are part of the contract. Let v,F:E->R and K a subset of E. Assume K is compact, tsupport(v) is contained in K and tsupport(F) is contained in K. Assume both v and F satisfy actual MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to volume, including volume-a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm.
Assume that for every real C2 compactly supported phi:E->R, both functions x->v(x)*Delta(phi)(x) and x->F(x)*phi(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral v(x)*Delta(phi)(x) dx = integral F(x)*phi(x) dx.
Here Delta(phi) is the actual test-function finite-basis Laplacian. No classical derivatives of v or F are assumed.
Then there exist vc,Fc in Lp C 2 volume such that vc=(x->(v(x):C)) volume-almost everywhere and Fc=(x->(F(x):C)) volume-almost everywhere. For these same vc,Fc all of the following conclusions hold simultaneously:
(1) For every psi in SchwartzMap E C, both x->Delta(psi)(x)*(v(x):C) and x->psi(x)*(F(x):C) are volume-integrable and
  integral Delta(psi)(x)*(v(x):C) dx = integral psi(x)*(F(x):C) dx.
(2) Delta(Lp.toTemperedDistribution(vc)) = Lp.toTemperedDistribution(Fc).
(3) MemSobolev 2 2 (Lp.toTemperedDistribution(vc)).
The classes are selected before all Schwartz tests and the complex test integrals use the original pointwise v and F casts, not newly selected functions per test. The real weak PDE and its two L1 products are premises; the two complex Schwartz L1 products, the complex test equation, the genuine distribution equation and Sobolev membership are conclusions.
Lp C 2 volume is the genuine complex L2 quotient with its standard measurable representative. These volume-a.e. identities bind the chosen classes to the actual pointwise real functions cast into C; they do not assert pointwise support identities for the chosen complex representatives. Every Schwartz test is a genuine smooth rapidly decreasing complex function on the real space E, and no compact-support restriction is imposed on it. Its derivatives are real Frechet derivatives. Pairings and displayed integrals use ordinary complex multiplication with no complex conjugation. Lp.toTemperedDistribution is the genuine complex-linear distribution embedding whose value at psi is integral psi(x)*the L2 representative(x) dx. The distribution Laplacian is the true tempered-distribution operator. MemSobolev 2 2 means there exists an actual fprime in Lp C 2 volume with besselPotential E C 2 of the displayed distribution equal to Lp.toTemperedDistribution(fprime); its multiplier is (1+||xi||^2)^(2/2). The approved Fourier convention is Delta T=-(2*pi)^2 FM(||xi||^2)T. This order-2 Bessel-Sobolev assertion is not a pointwise classical Laplacian, a real Hessian representative, or a weighted-core conclusion.

Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical ordinary Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for every x,a in E,
  alpha*||a||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x a) a <= beta*||a||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define the actual measures and potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g),mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
The tilted measure has density exp(-V)/integral exp(-V) against volume; the Gaussian is standard on the real Hilbert space, and prod and map are actual independent product and pushforward.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E with the following simultaneous properties: both are Markov kernels; R is a true conditional kernel disintegrating J.map Prod.swap; for every y in E, S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y in E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is Lebesgue integrable, and its Lebesgue integral is strictly positive. For this y there exists a real-linear partial operator D:L2(S(y);R)->L2(S(y);E), with dense domain in the actual scalar L2 space, D closable and D.closure closed. Its graph is exactly characterized by: for every scalar L2 class a and vector L2 class H, (a,H) belongs to graph(D) if and only if there exists a smooth compactly supported real function phi with a=phi S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For this same D, for every real epsilon>0 and every f in scalar L2(S(y)), there exists u in D.closure.domain satisfying all the following conclusions simultaneously. Let u_rep,f_rep be the standard representatives of the actual scalar L2 classes and G_rep the standard vector L2 representative of G=D.closure(u). Abbreviate the exact displayed scalar expression by
  r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W_y)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x).
(a) For every z in D.closure.domain,
  epsilon*<u,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(z)>_{L2(S(y);E)}=<f,z>_{L2(S(y);R)}.
(b) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to ordinary Lebesgue volume.
(c) For every real C1 compactly supported psi and every direction a in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),a>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
(d) x->||r(x)||^2, using the scalar real norm, is locally volume-integrable.
(e) For every compact K contained in E, u_rep,G_rep and r each satisfy MemLp at exponent 2 for volume.restrict K, including actual a.e. strong measurability and finite norm with respect to that restricted measure.
(f) For every real C2 compactly supported phi, both x->u_rep(x)*Delta(phi)(x) and x->r(x)*phi(x) are volume-integrable and
  integral u_rep(x)*Delta(phi)(x) dx = integral r(x)*phi(x) dx.
(g) For every real C2 compactly supported chi, define the following actual functions (v_chi denotes the statement's let-defined v):
  v_chi(x)=chi(x)*u_rep(x),
  G_chi(x)=chi(x) scalar-multiplied by G_rep(x) + u_rep(x) scalar-multiplied by gradient(chi)(x),
  F_chi(x)=chi(x)*r(x)+2*<gradient(chi)(x),G_rep(x)>_E+u_rep(x)*Delta(chi)(x).

For every real C1 compactly supported psi and a in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E and x->v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) are volume-integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_chi(x),a>_E dx = - integral v_chi(x)*(fderiv R psi x a) dx.
For every real C2 compactly supported phi, both x->v_chi(x)*Delta(phi)(x) and x->F_chi(x)*phi(x) are volume-integrable, and
  integral v_chi(x)*Delta(phi)(x) dx = integral F_chi(x)*phi(x) dx.
Furthermore for this chi there exist vc,Fc in Lp C 2 volume with vc=(x->(v_chi(x):C)) volume-almost everywhere and Fc=(x->(F_chi(x):C)) volume-almost everywhere, such that all the following hold for these same classes:
